answer: A fixed-pool dilution bond blocks bulk fakes. Each identity locks 70 credits and claims one dune plot. The beacon lists claims each epoch; the 40,000-credit pool is fixed and split equally, so fakes shrink all shares. Filing costs 40, then 40+8(k-1) per k-th: 1,000 fakes pay 4,036,000 plus 70,000 locked, each a 40-credit slice. A yarrow auditor replays claims; rented ones burn the bond. An honest agent files once, pays 40, keeps its share.
